summary: Alaska State Troopers reported two Monday arrests late on Monday evening: a Fairbanks woman arrested on a household assault charge and on a warrant a Fairbanks judge had issued four days earlier, and a man arrested on a felony drug warrant at the Tok trooper post and held at the Fairbanks jail. Nothing had been posted for Tuesday on either the trooper dispatch or the Fairbanks police bulletin at the time of reading. The court's weekly charges report now covers Nov. 17 to Nov. 23 and lists 42 criminal cases filed at Fairbanks and none at Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction; five of the 42 were opened with no charging document filed.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Julianna Nicholson
body: Julianna Nicholson, 29, of Fairbanks was arrested on charges of assault in the fourth degree, violating conditions of release, and an outstanding warrant. Assault in the fourth degree is recklessly injuring another person. Fairbanks, Nov. 23; Alaska State Troopers.
Troopers say they responded to a residence in Fairbanks for a report of a disturbance and determined that Nicholson had assaulted a household member and had also violated her conditions of release.

The warrant was issued on Nov. 19 by the Fairbanks court in case 4FA-26-01389CR, an open case in which Nicholson is charged with assault in the fourth degree, a Class A misdemeanor the court records as domestic violence related. Bail on the warrant was set at a $250 performance bond and a $500 unsecured appearance bond.

entries.title: Felony drug warrant arrest: Scott Kranenburg
body: Scott Richard Kranenburg was arrested on a felony warrant in case 3GL-26-00092CR, in which he is charged with misconduct involving a controlled substance in the third degree - manufacturing or delivering a controlled substance - a Class B felony, punishable by up to 10 years. A second count, endangering the welfare of a child in the second degree, is recorded by the court as a non-criminal violation.

Troopers say they contacted him at the Tok Trooper Post on Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. and arrested him on the warrant. He was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center on $1,000 bail, which the court record shows as posted.

The court records the offense at Glennallen on Feb. 22. The case was opened at the Glennallen court on Nov. 13 and arraignment is set for Dec. 1. Tok and Glennallen are outside the Fairbanks area this report covers; the arrest appears here because he was held at the Fairbanks jail.

entries.title: Assault and child-present charges: Emeline Janice Gallahorn
body: Emeline Janice Gallahorn is charged with assault in the fourth degree - recklessly injuring another person - and with six counts of assault when a child is present, all seven Class A misdemeanors. The court records all seven counts as domestic violence related.
Fairbanks, offense date Nov. 19. Case 4FA-26-02319CR, before Judge Maria P. Bahr. Nothing beyond the court record is reported here.

entries.title: Five Fairbanks cases opened in one week with no charging document filed
body: Five of the 42 criminal cases opened at the Fairbanks court between Nov. 17 and Nov. 23 carry a single entry recording a charging document as pending or not filed, and no charge or degree of offense. No charge has been brought in any of them.

4FA-26-02307CR, State of Alaska vs. Shay Pitka, offense date Nov. 18. 4FA-26-02316CR, State of Alaska vs. Katrina Albert, Nov. 19. 4FA-26-02317CR, State of Alaska vs. Arlo Charles Leroy Smoke, Nov. 19. 4FA-26-02320CR, State of Alaska vs. Felipe Soto Gomez, Nov. 20. 4FA-26-02337CR, State of Alaska vs. Shane Trevor O'Brien, Nov. 22.
The court's weekly disposed-cases report shows three of the five - the Pitka, Albert and Smoke cases - already closed, with no charge ever filed. The O'Brien case is set for arraignment on Nov. 27.
